source: psz-re — decompiled from arm9, tables read out of the ROM

room_name_builder.descriptor: param_1 is a 5-word struct: [0] stage number, [1] variant id, [2] shape id, [3] class id, [4] digit
room_name_builder.boss_variant: a second format, s%02dz_xxx at 0x020F9780, is built by FUN_0206D60C (982 bytes, called from 0x02050F8C)

variant.reading: 0=a 1=e 2=b 3=z are the four per-stage variants; 4..11 map to '0'..'7', which is how the final area's s080..s087 sub-stages are addressed

roles_confirmed_empirically.method: all 30 readable savestates on disk decoded statically with tools/mlstate.py (data/savestate_index.json) and grouped by the variant letter of their room codes
roles_confirmed_empirically.a: area A - room graphs of 8, 9 and 10 rooms
roles_confirmed_empirically.b: area B - room graphs of 8 rooms
roles_confirmed_empirically.e: single-room transition between areas; the one 'e' state is s01e_ia1, shape 'i' (2-door straight), matching kion's description of Valley E as a one-room link
roles_confirmed_empirically.z: boss arena - all 20 'z' states hold exactly ONE room and exactly one entity. s01z reads HP 1576/1650 with vtable 0x0219F8D4, which is Reyburn's HP and vtable as recorded from live GDB in an earlier iteration; s05z reads 5400/5400 with vtable 0x021A1604, the paru boss. That 'z' means boss was already inferred from the separate s%02dz format string in FUN_0206D60C; what is new is the empirical confirmation and the a/b/e roles.
roles_confirmed_empirically.caveat: no savestate exists for variants 0..7, so the s080..s087 reading is still untested

shape.reading: CONFIRMS the topology reading derived independently from NOF0 relocation counts. The table is ordered by connectivity: 0=i straight and 1=l corner are the 2-door shapes, 2=t is 3-door, 3=x is 4-door, then 4=n dead end, 5=s start and 6=g goal are the 1-door terminals.

class.reading: the second letter. Does not affect door count — ib1 and ic1 are both 2-door straights. Still unidentified; size or footprint class.
class.CORRECTION: the count of 4 is WRONG. The table at 0x020f24a8 reads 'abcdr' - FIVE entries - and class index 4 = 'r' is what forms the rare-room codes nr1..nr6. The byte at 0x020f24ac, previously unexplained between the class and shape tables, is that fifth letter.

validation: each mapper range-checks its id (0..11, 0..6, 0..3) and returns 0 on failure, so an out-of-range descriptor produces no name rather than a bad one
not_yet_known: what FILLS the descriptor. FUN_0206D2E4 only formats one that already exists. Its six callers are 0x0204005C, 0x020402A4, 0x020416DC and 0x02041918 among others; the selection logic and the seed are upstream of those and have not been traced.

loader.working_set: FUN_02050F8C zeroes three buffers before the loop: 0xA0 bytes of header, 0x1800 bytes and 0x1000 bytes, and passes 0x200 as the capacity for each of the latter two. 0x1800/512 = 12 bytes per entry and 0x1000/512 = 8 bytes per entry, so the layout is capped at 512 rooms.
loader.loop: FUN_0206D60C walks i from 0 to a count in its arg block. For each i it calls FUN_02032C10(descriptor, singleton, i) to FETCH a descriptor, FUN_0206D2E4 to format the name, and FUN_020401C8 to load it. It separately formats the boss room for the same stage with the s%02dz_xxx string. So this is the consumer: it reads a list that already exists.
loader.descriptor_source: FUN_02032C10, an accessor on the object at *0x0206D924

refuted.room_list_global: 0x02108C64, the value at DAT_0206D924, is NOT a room-list global. It is referenced from about 170 literal pools across arm9 and overlays 4, 12 and 17 — a general system singleton that many subsystems reach through. FUN_02032C10 is an accessor that indexes a member of it, so tracing writers to the global cannot isolate the generator. Recorded so the next attempt does not repeat it.

room_table.gate: FUN_02032C10 and its neighbours guard on a global at 0x0211A3C4, requiring *(that)+8 >= 0
room_table.base: *(*(0x02108C64)) — a DOUBLE indirection, resolved to 0x02243ED0 in all four field savestates
room_table.count: a 32-bit count at base + 0x410, bounds-checked as 0 <= i < count
room_table.descriptor: FUN_02041A08 copies exactly 5 words, so the record's first 20 bytes ARE the {stage, variantId, shapeId, classId, digit} descriptor; the remaining 32 bytes are other per-room data and are not yet identified
room_table.capacity_inferred: 0x410/0x34 = 20 exactly. Observed layouts run 8 to 10 rooms, so 20 as a ceiling is consistent but still not directly demonstrated.
room_table.not_the_512: the 0x200 capacities in FUN_02050F8C are for two OTHER per-room arrays of 12 and 8 bytes, not for this table. Room count and those buffers are separate things.
room_table.capacity_confirmed: 20, no longer an inference. FUN_020828D0 initialises the array with a loop that walks r4 from the base to base+0x410 in steps of 0x34, calling FUN_0208286C on each — exactly 20 iterations. Called from 0x020324C8.

verified: see data/level_layouts_observed.json — four real layouts read out of free-field savestates

writers.search: 0x410 is too large for a THUMB immediate offset, so every access must materialise it as mov rX,#0x41 ; lsl rX,#4. Scanning arm9 and all 32 overlays for that pair finds exactly 5 sites.

sites.0x02032E60: read — FUN_02032E5C, a bounds-checked record accessor returning base + i*0x34

writers.the_only_store: FUN_02082BE4(dest, src, kind) copies five words into dest[0..4], optionally a second descriptor at dest+0x34 when kind == 5, and writes param_1[0x104] — which is +0x410 — as 1 or 2. So it builds a one-or-two room list, NOT a generated field. Its callers are 0x02082B30, 0x02082BBC and 0x020831A0, and FUN_02082B30 does contain an RNG roll (FUN_020780F4 then FUN_0207816C) against a 5-entry threshold table, so this path is probabilistic — just not the field generator.

open_question: free fields hold 8 to 10 rooms, but the only +0x410 store in the binary writes 1 or 2. So the field count is written by something the offset search cannot see — a bulk copy of a prepared table, or a base pointer offset differently. NEXT: breakpoint FUN_020828D0, which runs when the table is constructed, and watch what fills it immediately afterwards. That sidesteps the static search entirely.
refuted_lead: the literal 0x00000410 appears once outside arm9, in ov16 at 0x02122620. It is DATA, not a code constant — the surrounding words are 0x320, 0x460, then negatives stepping by 352, a coordinate-shaped table. Not the generator.
